hash_convention: SHA-256 of UTF-8 json.dumps({subject: exact_subject, body: exact_body}, sort_keys=True, separators=(comma, colon), ensure_ascii=False). No whitespace or Unicode normalization is applied to either message string.

rubric_criteria.relevance: Does the message address the selected, evidence-supported objective?
rubric_criteria.clarity: Is the wording understandable and free from ambiguity?
rubric_criteria.personalization: Does it use appropriate verified context without unnecessary personal data?
rubric_criteria.call_to_action: Is the next step clear and proportionate, including no required action for appreciation?
rubric_criteria.tone: Is it respectful and appropriate for the selected objective and reminder stage?

method: The assistant read each exact subject/body, selected strategy, raw verified customer context and relevant offer catalogue entry before assigning independent criterion scores. Scores are qualitative judgments, not validation-rule pass counts or authority to deliver.
overall_limitations: These six selected synthetic examples are not representative of telecom customer prevalence or the full 5,000-customer fixture.
All reviewed messages were generated by local deterministic templates; no Astra or other OpenAI generation output was assessed.
This is a single automated assistant assessment, not human feedback, a blinded study, an inter-rater reliability result, or evidence of customer satisfaction.
No real delivery, activation, payment, support journey, conversion, or user comprehension outcome was observed.
Correct selected-policy content can coexist with weak personalization and an impractical CTA. Missing approved contact destinations cannot safely be replaced by invented links or numbers.
Every score applies only to the exact hashed message and supplied historical facts; edited content or changed evidence requires reassessment.

rationales.relevance: The subject and body deliver appreciation without an offer, matching the selected strategy and the active customer with three timely settled invoices.
rationales.clarity: The short sentences are easy to understand, but the two consecutive expressions of gratitude repeat the same idea.
rationales.personalization: Only the greeting is individualized. The verified eight-month relationship is not reflected, so the message could be sent unchanged to almost any customer; adding sensitive billing detail would not improve this appreciation note.
rationales.call_to_action: No required action is appropriate for appreciation. The optional support invitation is proportionate but gives no concrete support route.
rationales.tone: Warm, respectful and free of pressure, unsupported benefits, or intrusive references to customer behaviour.

assessments.overall_assessment: A clear, appropriate thank-you note with weak personalization and some repetition.
overall_limitations: No customer has rated whether this generic appreciation feels meaningful.
No approved support destination is supplied, so the optional support invitation cannot be made operational from these facts alone.

rationales.relevance: The exact selected active offer applies to POSTPAID_499; the 2GB benefit, 30-day validity, 90-day restriction and expiry match the supplied catalogue. The customer has 24 months of tenure and no recorded prior redemption.
rationales.clarity: The benefit and terms are visible, but the versioned synthetic title, the term provisioning, and a UTC expiry introduce prototype and technical language into customer-facing copy.
rationales.personalization: The greeting and generic reference to a mobile plan are the only tailoring. The verified two-year relationship is not acknowledged, and the copy is otherwise identical to the decline and dormant samples.
rationales.call_to_action: The customer is invited to discuss the offer, and the text correctly says it is not activated. However, usual channel names no route and does not explain how to request the offer using its code.
rationales.tone: Polite and unpressured, but the catalogue-style wording is transactional and does little to convey appreciation for loyalty.

assessments.overall_assessment: Factually relevant offer copy that needs clearer customer wording, meaningful loyalty recognition, and an approved next-step route.
overall_limitations: The offer is synthetic and cannot actually be provisioned; this review does not demonstrate redemption usability or conversion.
Improving catalogue wording or adding a support route requires approved source content, not an invented link or promise.

rationales.relevance: The message presents the approved offer chosen for this customer, with benefit, terms and expiry matching the eligible POSTPAID_799 catalogue entry. It avoids claiming an unsupported reason for reduced activity.
rationales.clarity: The structured fact lines are readable, but the synthetic version title, provisioning terminology and UTC expiry need clearer customer-facing presentation.
rationales.personalization: Apart from the name, this is the same message as the loyalty and dormant offers. It does not use the verified plan context or offer helpful context for the recorded allowance question; the decline from 27 to five active days does not establish why usage fell.
rationales.call_to_action: An invitation to discuss the offer is acceptable, but usual channel is vague and there is no concrete approved support path or instruction to reference the offer code.
rationales.tone: Respectful and nonjudgmental. It does not shame reduced usage or infer dissatisfaction, although the tone is generic rather than especially helpful.

assessments.overall_assessment: Accurate selected-offer content with little evidence of tailoring to this engagement situation.
overall_limitations: Lower activity does not establish churn intent, negative sentiment, or that extra data will be useful.
No customer response or approved support-route usability test is available.

rationales.relevance: The selected offer is eligible for the active POSTPAID_499 subscription and all stated terms match the catalogue. The message stays within the chosen offer objective without asserting a reason for inactivity.
rationales.clarity: Benefit and restrictions are laid out, but the technical version label, no-actual-provisioning wording and UTC expiry reduce clarity for a normal telecom customer.
rationales.personalization: Only the name differentiates this from the other offer samples. The copy contains no tailored, optional help or welcome-back framing, despite a complete current window with zero active days; that fact alone would not justify claiming the customer has left.
rationales.call_to_action: It makes clear that activation has not occurred, but asks only for discussion through an unspecified usual channel. A usable approved support route and concrete next step are missing.
rationales.tone: Courteous and low pressure, appropriately avoiding blame or assumptions about inactivity. It remains generic rather than particularly welcoming.

assessments.overall_assessment: A safe, relevant offer presentation with weak re-engagement usefulness and an incomplete practical CTA.
overall_limitations: Zero observed activity does not prove cancellation, dissatisfaction, or a need for more data.
The synthetic offer and unspecified contact route prevent assessing real reactivation success.

rationales.relevance: The named invoice, INR 350 outstanding and 2026-11-12 due date match the selected partially paid invoice. The message correctly requests attention to the remaining balance rather than the full INR 700 original amount.
rationales.clarity: The invoice, amount and due date are easy to find. The self-description courteous reminder and repeated support phrasing could be tightened.
rationales.personalization: The greeting and exact invoice, remaining balance and due date use directly relevant verified context without exposing account, subscription or contact details.
rationales.call_to_action: Reviewing the balance and contacting support for payment/dispute questions are proportionate, but usual billing channel and usual channel do not tell the customer where to act or how to resolve a verified unpaid balance.
rationales.tone: Appropriately courteous for a first reminder, with room for payment reconciliation or dispute and no threatening or shaming language.

assessments.overall_assessment: A well-grounded and respectful first reminder; a concrete approved billing/support route is the main practical gap.
overall_limitations: The amount and payment state are correct only at the supplied reference time; fresh checks remain necessary before any delivery.
No real customer has tested the billing or dispute path, and this template provides no approved destination.

rationales.relevance: The INR 1200 balance, invoice identifier and 2026-10-26 due date match the selected invoice. At the reference time, the two recorded reminders on November 1 and 9 support the selected third-stage follow-up.
rationales.clarity: The factual block is easy to scan, but the opening needs-attention wording is generic and the repeated support language could be more concise.
rationales.personalization: The customer name and invoice facts are correct and relevant. The text does not acknowledge that this is a follow-up to verified earlier reminders, so stage-specific context appears only indirectly through the firmer wording.
rationales.call_to_action: The balance-review and dispute options remain proportionate, but the same unspecified usual-channel CTA as the first reminder leaves the practical next step unclear. A new deadline or penalty should not be invented to compensate.
rationales.tone: Firm enough to signal follow-up while remaining respectful, supportive and free of unsupported consequences or threats.

assessments.overall_assessment: An accurate, appropriately firm reminder whose practical CTA and follow-up context could be stronger.
overall_limitations: The prior reminders and outstanding balance are historical snapshot facts, not proof the debt remains outstanding now.
This review does not test recipient response, collectability, or legal/compliance suitability for a live billing campaign.
